successCriteria.description: The `LeaveRequestStatus` enum is exported from `src/shared/types/leave.types.ts` with exactly five members: `DRAFT`, `SUBMITTED`, `APPROVED`, `REJECTED`, `CANCELLED` — matching the reconciled architecture lifecycle.

The `LeaveType` enum is exported from `src/shared/types/leave.types.ts` with exactly six members: `annual`, `sick`, `emergency`, `unpaid`, `maternity`, `paternity` — matching the reconciled architecture.

The `AuditAction` enum is exported from `src/shared/types/leave.types.ts` with exactly seven members: `CREATED`, `UPDATED`, `DELETED`, `APPROVED`, `REJECTED`, `CANCELLED`, `SUBMITTED` — covering every state-changing operation the audit module must record.

The `BaseEntity` type is exported from `src/shared/types/leave.types.ts` with exactly three fields: `id: string`, `createdAt: Date`, `updatedAt: Date` — providing the canonical base shape for all domain entities.

The barrel file `src/shared/types/index.ts` re-exports every named export from `leave.types.ts` — `LeaveRequestStatus`, `LeaveType`, `AuditAction`, and `BaseEntity` — so that downstream modules can import from `shared/types` without reaching into the internal file.

A Jest unit test file at `tests/unit/shared/types/leave.types.test.ts` verifies that each enum's runtime values match the canonical member names (e.g. `LeaveRequestStatus.DRAFT === 'DRAFT'`, `LeaveType.annual === 'annual'`, `AuditAction.CREATED === 'CREATED'`). The test file uses the `.test.ts` extension matching the existing `jest.config.js` `testMatch` pattern.

constraints: The test file MUST use the `.test.ts` extension (not `.spec.ts`) — the existing `jest.config.js` matches only `**/tests/**/*.test.(ts|js)`. Using `.spec.ts` would cause the test to be silently skipped.

All TypeScript enums must use string values (not numeric) — the canonical values are the member names themselves (e.g. `DRAFT = 'DRAFT'`). This ensures serialization consistency across the stack and readable audit records.

The `BaseEntity` type must be a TypeScript `type` (not an `interface` or `class`) — it is a structural shape, not a nominal contract. Downstream entities extend it via intersection (`&`) or structural compatibility.
No `any` type anywhere — per HARNESS.json constraint `no-any`. Use `unknown` with type guards if needed.
Imports within `src/shared/types/` must use the `baseUrl`-relative paths (e.g. `shared/types/leave.types`) as configured in `tsconfig.json` (`baseUrl: "./src"`).
outOfScope: Database tables, migrations, or Knex schema definitions — this phase is pure TypeScript types with zero runtime dependencies.
Any domain entity beyond the enums and BaseEntity — LeaveRequest, LeaveBalance, LeavePolicy, Employee, AuditLog, and Notification entities are defined in their respective module phases (2–6).
Repository interfaces, service interfaces, DTOs, or any runtime logic — this phase is exclusively type definitions and enum declarations.

entityInvariants.invariant: The enum defines exactly five states: DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED. These are the only valid states for a LeaveRequest. The allowed transitions are: DRAFT → SUBMITTED; SUBMITTED → APPROVED | REJECTED; DRAFT | SUBMITTED | APPROVED → CANCELLED. REJECTED and CANCELLED are terminal. No other transitions are valid — this is enforced by downstream service logic, but the enum itself must not contain any state outside this set.

The enum defines exactly six leave categories: annual, sick, emergency, unpaid, maternity, paternity. Each type carries its own entitlement pool and policy rules. No leave type may be added or removed without a corresponding policy definition.

The enum defines exactly seven actions: CREATED, UPDATED, DELETED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED, SUBMITTED. Every state-changing operation on LeaveRequest or LeaveBalance must map to one of these actions in the audit record (GP-002).

Every domain entity (LeaveRequest, LeaveBalance, LeavePolicy, Employee, AuditLog) must be structurally compatible with BaseEntity — it must have `id: string`, `createdAt: Date`, and `updatedAt: Date`. This is the canonical base shape; downstream entities satisfy it either by explicit intersection or by declaring the same fields.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The `LeaveRequestStatus` enum members (DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED) must match the domain entity definition in the reconciled architecture — no extra states, no missing states, no renamed states.

The `LeaveType` enum members (annual, sick, emergency, unpaid, maternity, paternity) must match the domain entity definition in the reconciled architecture — no extra types, no missing types, no renamed types.

The `AuditAction` enum members (CREATED, UPDATED, DELETED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED, SUBMITTED) must cover every state transition operation described in the reconciled architecture's business rules — specifically rules 2 (state transitions), 4 (approval), 5 (cancellation), 8 (termination cascade), and 9 (audit requirement).
